name: v100
description: NVIDIA Tesla V100 SXM2 (GV100, Volta, sm_70) at its 1530 MHz boost clock: one Vortex core per SM.

sources.NUM_CORES, NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE: 80 SMs, 64 resident warps/SM, 4 processing blocks with one scheduler each (NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture whitepaper, Table 1)
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS, L2_NUM_BANKS: 6 MB L2 (whitepaper), rounded down to the power of two the cache accepts; 16 ways, 32 banks for the 32 memory channels
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 4 HBM2 stacks x 8 128-bit channels = 32 channels at 1752 MT/s: 32 x 16 B x 1752 MT/s = 897 GB/s (whitepaper)
sources.FETCH_WIDTH: 4 SM processing blocks, each with its own warp scheduler, dispatch unit and L0 instruction cache (NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture whitepaper)
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client, so uploaded data is L2-resident at launch
sources.LMEM_LOG_SIZE, DCACHE_SIZE: 96 KB maximum shared memory per SM (CUDA Programming Guide, compute capability 7.0), rounded down to the power of two the LMEM accepts. DCACHE_SIZE keeps the whole 128 KB L1/shared pool: the driver gives a kernel the L1 its shared-memory use leaves, so a kernel without shared memory sees the full pool
sources.LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 32 shared-memory banks of 4 B, as on every NVIDIA GPU since Maxwell (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, shared memory)
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: Every NVIDIA GPU since Pascal has a demand-paged MMU (unified memory), global and shared-memory atomics with a native compare-and-swap (atomicCAS), FP16 storage and conversion, and per-partition special-function units for the transcendentals (MUFU)
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE, TCU_*, EXT_DXA_ENABLE, E: Volta tensor cores: FP16 inputs with FP32 accumulation only (Volta whitepaper). The TCU's FP16 format group also carries BF16, which Volta lacks: no knob separates them
sources.xlen: 64-bit machine: 64-bit pointers and FP64 (the D extension follows XLEN=64), with a 48-bit device address space against NVIDIA's 49-bit virtual addresses; configure --profile picks a build64 tree and a build32 tree rejects the profile
sources.NUM_BARRIERS: 16 named CTA barriers (bar.sync 0-15, PTX ISA) on every NVIDIA GPU
sources.EXT_RASTER_ENABLE, EXT_OM_ENABLE: Raster engines in every GPC and ROPs in every memory partition (architecture whitepaper)
sources.NUM_MUFU_LANES: 16 special-function results per clock per SM (4 SFUs in each of the 4 processing blocks) for the reciprocal, reciprocal square root, log2, exp2, sine and cosine (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 7.0)
sources.SIMD_WIDTH: Left at NUM_THREADS (32) although the part has 16 FP32 / 16 INT32 lanes per SM processing block, so a warp instruction issues over two cycles (Volta whitepaper): the RTL TCU needs full-warp operands (NUM_TCU_LANES == NUM_THREADS) and VX_lane_dispatch cannot widen a 16-lane dispatch to 32 lanes, so SIMD_WIDTH=16 with EXT_TCU_ENABLE does not build in rtlsim. The tensor cores are kept; the ALU/FPU/LSU issue width is 2x the part's
